docs.title: RepoAtlas
docs.text: RepoAtlas builds a local, persistent structural index for Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, and Java repositories. It exposes ranked source maps and dependency queries through a CLI and optional MCP server.

docs.title: What it provides
docs.text:
• Incremental SQLite indexing with stable symbol identifiers.
  • Symbol, caller, callee, impact, and bounded context queries.
  • Optional shared daemon for multiple local clients.
  • Configurable file exclusions and output redaction.
  • Git-history parity checks and offline retrieval estimates.

Start with installation, then review architecture and project structure, configuration, and the CLI/MCP tools.

docs.title: Architecture and Project Structure
docs.text: RepoAtlas uses a src-based Python package layout. Runtime code lives under src/repo_atlas; tests, documentation, and benchmark inputs stay outside the installable package. This keeps the distribution boundary explicit and lets tests exercise the installed package rather than accidentally importing files from the repository root.

docs.title: Repository map
docs.text:
.
|-- src/repo_atlas/       Installable application package
|-- tests/                Automated tests, grouped by behavior
|-- docs/                 User and maintainer documentation
|-- bench/                Offline benchmark task manifests
|-- .github/workflows/    Continuous integration
|-- pyproject.toml        Packaging, dependencies, and tool configuration
|-- ratlas.toml.example   Example repository configuration
|-- README.md             Project overview and quick start

The main package modules have distinct responsibilities:

Module Responsibility cli.py Typer commands and command-line orchestration server.py Optional, read-only MCP tools, resources, and prompts config.py Configuration models, defaults, and validation indexer.py File discovery, incremental updates, and index coordination parser.py Language-specific structural extraction models.py Shared records used across parsing, indexing, and storage diff.py Symbol change and rename matching resolver.py Reference resolution, including optional SCIP mappings store.py SQLite schema, transactions, locks, and persistence engine.py Search, ranking, graph queries, redaction, and context rendering daemon.py Local shared-index process and client requests benchmark.py Offline retrieval benchmark execution and reports replay.py Incremental-versus-full indexing checks across Git history

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
CLI or MCP request
        |
        +--> load and validate configuration
        |
        +--> Indexer --> discover eligible files --> parser --> symbols/references
        |                     |                                      |
        |                     +------ incremental changes ------------+
        |                                                            |
        +--> ContextEngine <------------------------------ SQLiteStore
                 |
                 +--> ranked, bounded, redacted results

The CLI and MCP server are adapters: they translate external requests into calls to the indexing, storage, and query layers. The indexer coordinates work but delegates parsing, symbol matching, reference resolution, and persistence to their respective modules. The query engine reads the persisted index and shapes results; callers should not reach into SQLite directly for user-facing queries. The optional daemon shares indexing work between local clients but does not change the stored data model.

docs.title: Extension conventions
docs.text:
• Keep command and protocol code at the edges. Put reusable behavior in the owning domain module so it can be called and tested without starting a CLI or server.
  • Keep parsing deterministic and return the shared records in models.py; do not make parsers write to the database.
  • Put schema and transaction behavior in store.py. Changes to persisted data must account for schema versioning and existing index files.
  • Add tests beside the behavior they protect, using temporary repositories and databases. Prefer public behavior over assertions on private implementation details.
  • Keep optional integrations optional. Import an integration only when it is used and provide an actionable message when its extra is missing.
  • Add a new module when it gives a domain a clear owner. Split a module into a package when the domain has multiple independently understandable components; avoid moving files only to make the tree look larger.

docs.title: Quality checks
docs.text:
Run the test and packaging checks from the repository root after installing the development extra. Install the documentation extra to build the site:

python -m pytest
ratlas replay --commits 50
python -m pip wheel --no-deps --wheel-dir dist .
python -m pip install -e ".[docs]"
python -m mkdocs build --strict

CI currently runs the test suite, Git-history replay check, and wheel build. Ruff and mypy are configured in pyproject.toml; add them to the development dependencies and CI before treating them as required checks. Keep CI changes in sync with the checks documented here when adding or replacing tooling.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
ratlas init writes a starter ratlas.toml. See the complete sample configuration, also available as ratlas.toml.example in the repository root.

  • index.languages: enabled parser families (python, typescript, java).
  • index.include and index.exclude: repository-relative glob patterns.
  • index.max_file_bytes: skip larger source files.
  • index.bulk_threshold_pct: percentage triggering a global edge rebuild.
  • resolve.confidence_floor: minimum edge confidence for relationship traversal.
  • resolve.precise_provider: none or scip normalized mapping provider.
  • privacy.never_index: paths excluded before reading source.
  • privacy.redact_patterns: regular expressions applied to returned text.
  • budget.*: response limits and conservative token estimate settings.
  • store.path: SQLite database file or directory.

SCIP mappings use JSON entries identifying the source file/symbol/reference and target file/qualified name. Generate the map with an external language-specific SCIP integration; RepoAtlas does not parse SCIP protobuf directly.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.11 or later.

py -3.11 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -e ".[dev,mcp]"

From a target repository:

ratlas init
ratlas index
ratlas query map
ratlas query context "trace request handling" --budget 4000

To build the documentation locally, install .[docs] and run mkdocs serve.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
RepoAtlas 1.0.0 is a useful navigation index, not a compiler or IDE language server.

  • Python uses the standard-library AST with best-effort partial recovery.
  • TypeScript/JavaScript and Java use structural scanning; modern syntax and malformed files can be missed or misclassified.
  • Reference resolution is heuristic except for configured normalized SCIP mappings.
  • Token counts use a byte-based estimate and can differ from model tokenizer counts.
  • Offline benchmark reports retrieval estimates only; assistant execution, dollar costs, and pass rates are not measured.
  • The real-history replay command requires a Git repository with commits.
  • This release does not include an LSP/SCIP protobuf importer, alternate graph store, embedding search, or hosted service.

Verify all impact results and symbol ranges against the source repository before making changes.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• TypeScript/JavaScript and Java parsing is structural scanning, not language-server/compiler parsing. Complex syntax, decorators/annotations, overloads, and malformed code can be missed.
  • Python partial recovery keeps declarations around damaged ranges but cannot guarantee full fidelity during arbitrary edits.
  • Without a normalized SCIP mapping, symbol resolution is heuristic. Impact results are hints, not proof of breakage.
  • Token counts use a conservative byte proxy. They are not exact counts for a specific model tokenizer.
  • The offline benchmark compares retrieval estimates only. It does not drive an assistant, execute task tests, or establish success@1 or cost savings.
  • The SCIP integration accepts a normalized JSON mapping produced externally; it does not invoke SCIP or read protobuf indexes.
  • Daemon transport is authenticated loopback TCP; named-pipe transport and robust service-manager integration are not included.
  • No embedding service, remote index, alternate graph store, or cross-repository search is included.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Useful commands:

  • ratlas index [--full]: build or reconcile the local index.
  • ratlas query map --budget 2000: print a repository overview.
  • ratlas query context "task" --focus src/file.py: retrieve task context.
  • ratlas query symbol NAME [--kind function]: find symbol definitions.
  • ratlas callers TARGET, ratlas callees TARGET, and ratlas impact TARGET: inspect graph relationships.
  • ratlas daemon start|status|stop: share an index writer locally.
  • ratlas replay --commits 50: compare incremental and fresh graphs over Git history.
  • ratlas bench run --tasks bench/tasks.json: produce offline A/B/C retrieval estimates.

The benchmark does not run an assistant or infer task success. It reports that field as unmeasured.

docs.title: MCP
docs.text:
Install the mcp extra and configure a stdio server that runs ratlas serve with the repository as its working directory. Tools: repo_map, get_context, find_symbol, get_symbol, callers_of, callees_of, impact_of, and index_status. Resource: ratlas://map. Prompt: ratlas-onboard.

The surface is read-only. Freshness requests reconcile via the shared daemon when running and otherwise index in the server process.
